maastricht-university.about:
Founded in 1976, Maastricht University (UM) sits in a historic city on the Belgian and German borders and has one of the highest shares of international students in Europe. All teaching follows Problem-Based Learning in tutorial groups of about 12–15 students, and most bachelor's programmes are in English, including International Business, Economics and Business Economics, European Law School, European Studies, Psychology, Data Science, Health Sciences and University College Maastricht.

Applicants register via Studielink and the UM portal; deadlines depend on whether a programme is free, selective or fixus. Non-EU/EEA students pay institutional fees (from €13,400 in 2027/28) plus a €100 handling fee.
maastricht-university.aid_intl: Limited merit scholarships for non-EEA students (e.g. UM Holland-High Potential and Holland Scholarship).
maastricht-university.tests: No SAT/ACT. English-taught programmes require English proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge as specified per programme); some programmes need maths at a set level. Selective and fixus programmes add a selection procedure.
maastricht-university.gpa_note: Diploma equivalent to Dutch VWO with required subjects; selective programmes assess grades and motivation.
requirements: Secondary school diploma equivalent to Dutch VWO
Motivation letter/selection tasks for selective programmes
Proof of funds for the residence permit

macquarie-university-sydney-australia.about:
Founded in 1964, Macquarie University sits on a large green campus in Macquarie Park, alongside a business park home to many tech and pharmaceutical companies. It is known for actuarial studies, applied finance, linguistics, psychology, earth and environmental sciences, and media, and has its own private hospital.

International applicants apply online with their secondary results and English scores (IELTS 6.5 with 6.0 bands for most courses). Applications are assessed on a rolling basis for February and July starts, and merit scholarships are offered.
macquarie-university-sydney-australia.aid_intl: Merit scholarships such as the Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarship (partial tuition).
macquarie-university-sydney-australia.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general; entry by secondary qualification. English (most undergraduate courses): IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band; some courses (e.g. Laws, Clinical Science, Exercise and Sports Science) require 7.0 with 6.5 per band.
macquarie-university-sydney-australia.gpa_note: Course-specific entry ranks converted from your qualification.
requirements: English test at the course's level
Proof of funds for the Australian student visa

massey-university.about:
Massey University has campuses in Palmerston North (Manawatū), Auckland and Wellington, plus a large distance-learning offer. It is New Zealand's only provider of veterinary science alongside strong agriculture, food technology and aviation (including a professional pilot pathway), and its Wellington College of Creative Arts is a leading design school.

International students apply directly online, meeting entrance requirements for their qualification and English at IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5.5) for undergraduate study. Semester 1 begins in late February, and merit scholarships are available.
massey-university.aid_intl: International merit scholarships (partial tuition), e.g. Massey University International Excellence Scholarships.
massey-university.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement in general. English for undergraduate study: Academic IELTS 6.0 overall with at least 5.5 in each band (IELTS Online accepted), or equivalent TOEFL/Duolingo scores; some qualifications have higher requirements.
massey-university.gpa_note: Entry by your secondary qualification (equivalent to NZ University Entrance); veterinary science and aviation are selective.
requirements: English test (programme level; IELTS 6.0 with no band below 5.5 is typical)
Proof of funds for the New Zealand student visa

nagoya-university.about:
Nagoya University is one of Japan's seven former imperial universities, with its main Higashiyama campus in Nagoya. It is especially strong in physics, chemistry, biology, engineering (including automotive and aerospace, given the Toyota-centred Chubu economy), agriculture and medicine.

Since 2011 its G30 International Programs have offered full English-taught bachelor's degrees in fields such as automotive engineering, physics, chemistry, biological science, social sciences and Japanese culture, starting in October with Japanese-language training. Tuition is the low national-university rate, and MEXT and university scholarships plus fee exemptions help further.
nagoya-university.aid_intl: MEXT and JASSO scholarships, university scholarships and tuition/admission-fee exemptions for international students.
nagoya-university.tests: G30 International Programs (English-taught) are selective and use document screening with standardized test results and English proficiency; exact minimums are set in the G30 application guidelines. Japanese-taught programmes require Japanese fluency and the EJU/school-specific exams.
nagoya-university.gpa_note: Selective document review; strong maths and science results expected for science/engineering tracks.
requirements: Secondary school diploma (12 years of schooling)
Standardized test results as specified by G30 (e.g. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level)

pohang-university-of-science-and-technol.about:
POSTECH was founded in 1986 by POSCO as Korea's first research-oriented university and remains small (roughly 1,400 undergraduates), with a high faculty-to-student ratio. It is strongest in materials science, chemistry and chemical engineering, physics (with the Pohang Accelerator Laboratory), life sciences and computer science.

International applicants apply online with transcripts, recommendation letters and essays, followed by document review and interviews if necessary. The university operates as a bilingual campus with most courses in English, and scholarships are widely available.
pohang-university-of-science-and-technol.aid_intl: Generous scholarships: POSTECH scholarships and Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) for international undergraduates.
pohang-university-of-science-and-technol.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement stated; selection by document review and, if necessary, interview. Strong maths and science records and English proficiency are expected; exact minimums are in POSTECH's admission guideline.
pohang-university-of-science-and-technol.gpa_note: Very strong mathematics and science preparation is expected.
requirements: Financial documents for the D-2 visa

queen-s-university-belfast.about:
Founded in 1845, Queen's University Belfast is Northern Ireland's leading research university and a member of the Russell Group. Its campus in south Belfast hosts faculties of medicine, health and life sciences, engineering and physical sciences, and arts, humanities and social sciences, with notable strength in cybersecurity (CSIT), pharmacy and law.

International undergraduates apply through UCAS (Q75) with predicted grades, a personal statement and a reference; medicine and dentistry need the UCAT and an earlier October deadline. 2027/28 international fees start at £24,600, and merit scholarships reduce tuition for many entrants.
queen-s-university-belfast.aid_intl: Merit-based international scholarships (partial tuition discounts) for undergraduate entrants; no need-based aid.
queen-s-university-belfast.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement (US applicants may use SAT/AP for entry). English: IELTS Academic 6.0 with at least 5.5 in each component for most degrees (6.5 for some courses); TOEFL iBT accepted. Medicine and Dentistry require the UCAT.
queen-s-university-belfast.gpa_note: Typical offers range from ABB to A*AA at A-level (or IB equivalents) depending on the course.
requirements: English test (IELTS 6.0, min 5.5 per component, or course-specific)
Proof of funds for the UK Student visa (CAS)

radboud-university.about:
Radboud University, founded in 1923, has a green campus in Nijmegen alongside the Radboud university medical center and the Donders Institute for brain research. It offers bachelor's programmes in psychology, artificial intelligence, communication science, international business, economics, law, philosophy, theology, sciences and arts, a growing number in English.

International students apply through Studielink; numerus fixus programmes close on 15 January and other programmes on 1 April for non-EU/EEA students. English requirements are firm (IELTS 6.0 with every band 6.0, or TOEFL 80 with every section 20).
radboud-university.aid_intl: Radboud Scholarship Programme and Holland Scholarship (partial), mainly for non-EEA students.
radboud-university.tests: No SAT/ACT. English (bachelor's): IELTS Academic 6.0 with all sub-scores 6.0 (IELTS Online not accepted; One Skill Retake accepted); TOEFL iBT 80 with all sub-scores 20 (or 4.5 on the new scale; Home Edition not accepted); Cambridge C1 Advanced 169.
radboud-university.gpa_note: Diploma comparable to Dutch VWO with subject requirements; numerus fixus programmes rank applicants.
requirements: Secondary school diploma comparable to Dutch VWO
English test (IELTS 6.0, all sub-scores 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 80, all 20 / Cambridge C1 169)
Studielink registration; selection for numerus fixus programmes
Proof of funds for the residence permit

rutgers-universitynew-brunswick.about:
Chartered in 1766, Rutgers is one of the oldest universities in the US and a Big Ten member. The New Brunswick campus is the largest of its three, with schools of arts and sciences, engineering, business, pharmacy, nursing, environmental and biological sciences, and the arts, about an hour from New York City.

International first-years apply online with transcripts (self-reported via STARS) and English proficiency evidence; tests are optional. Applying by 1 December ensures merit-scholarship consideration, though need-based aid is not available to internationals.
rutgers-universitynew-brunswick.aid_intl: Merit-based scholarships (consideration requires applying by 1 December); no federal need-based aid for international students.
rutgers-universitynew-brunswick.tests: SAT/ACT optional for most programmes. English proficiency required if schooling was outside an English-speaking country: TOEFL iBT 79 (tests to 21 Jan 2026) or 4.5 on the new scale; IELTS 6.5 (6.0 for some schools); MET 56; or SAT EBRW 550 / ACT English; Duolingo also accepted. Waivers possible for English-medium schools.
rutgers-universitynew-brunswick.gpa_note: Holistic academic review; competitive schools (engineering, business, pharmacy) expect strong maths and science grades.
requirements: Self-reported academic record (STARS), official transcripts if admitted
English test (TOEFL iBT 79 / IELTS 6.5 / Duolingo / MET 56) unless waived
Portfolio/audition for Mason Gross School of the Arts
Financial documents for the I-20/F-1 visa

shandong-university.about:
Shandong University, founded in 1901, is one of China's oldest modern universities, with campuses in Jinan, Qingdao and Weihai in Confucius's home province. It is strong in mathematics, chemistry and crystal materials, medicine, and Chinese literature, history and philosophy.

International undergraduates apply with school records, HSK (or English scores for English-taught options such as MBBS) and a CSCA report. CSC and Shandong provincial scholarships are available.
shandong-university.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
shandong-university.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
shandong-university.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

sichuan-university.about:
Sichuan University, with roots in 1896, is one of western China's largest research universities, with campuses in Chengdu. Its West China School of Stomatology and West China Hospital are among the best in China, and it is also strong in polymer materials, mathematics, Chinese literature and history.

International undergraduates apply online with school records, a CSCA report and HSK for Chinese-taught degrees (or English scores where English-taught options exist). CSC and Sichuan provincial scholarships are available.
sichuan-university.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
sichuan-university.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
sichuan-university.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

southern-university-of-science-and-techn.about:
SUSTech is a public research university founded by the Shenzhen government in 2011 to pioneer reform in Chinese higher education. Located in China's tech capital, it focuses on physics, materials, computer science, biomedical engineering, mathematics and earth sciences, with small classes and a high share of English-taught courses.

International undergraduates apply online with school records, English proficiency and a CSCA report; selection may include interviews. Scholarships are available for strong applicants.
southern-university-of-science-and-techn.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
southern-university-of-science-and-techn.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
southern-university-of-science-and-techn.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

stockholm-university.about:
Stockholm University, founded in 1878, has its main Frescati campus in the Royal National City Park in northern Stockholm. It is a broad research university known for the social sciences (economics, political science, criminology), law, the Stockholm Resilience Centre, and natural sciences including physics, astronomy and environmental science.

Most bachelor's programmes are in Swedish; English-taught options at bachelor's level are limited, while the master's offer is large. International applicants apply via universityadmissions.se in the first round (deadline 15 January) with transcripts, proof of English 6 and, for non-EU/EEA citizens, the application fee and later tuition.
stockholm-university.aid_intl: Few or no bachelor's-level scholarships; Swedish Institute scholarships are for master's students. Some universities offer partial tuition waivers to fee-paying students.
stockholm-university.tests: No SAT/ACT. Swedish-taught programmes require Swedish 3; English-taught programmes require English 6 (typically IELTS Academic 6.5 with no section below 5.5, or TOEFL iBT 90 with writing 20). Programme-specific maths/science prerequisites apply.
stockholm-university.gpa_note: Selection mainly by upper-secondary grades (merit rating) when programmes are oversubscribed.
requirements: English 6 (e.g. IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 90) or Swedish 3, depending on the programme
Proof of funds for the Swedish residence permit

sun-yat-sen-university.about:
Founded by Dr Sun Yat-sen in 1924, SYSU is one of southern China's leading universities, with campuses in Guangzhou, Zhuhai and Shenzhen. It is particularly strong in medicine (with several affiliated hospitals), business, marine sciences, chemistry, and the social sciences.

International undergraduates apply online with school records, a CSCA report and HSK for Chinese-taught programmes (or English scores for English-taught ones such as clinical medicine). CSC, Guangdong and university scholarships are offered.
sun-yat-sen-university.aid_intl: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) and university/provincial scholarships for international students; English-taught and self-funded programmes may have separate awards.
sun-yat-sen-university.tests: From the 2026/27 intake every international undergraduate applicant to Chinese universities must submit a CSCA (China Scholastic Competency Assessment) report (national requirement run by the China Scholarship Council; tests held several times a year). Chinese-taught programmes require an HSK certificate (typically HSK 4–5 with 180+ depending on the major); English-taught programmes require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. SAT/ACT/IB/A-level results can support an application but are not required. Exact thresholds are set in the university's annual admissions guide.
sun-yat-sen-university.gpa_note: Selection on senior-high record, language level, CSCA results and (where used) interview or written test.
requirements: High school diploma or expected graduation certificate
Interview or written test if required

sungkyunkwan-university-skku.about:
Sungkyunkwan University traces its origins to the Joseon dynasty's royal academy and is today a private research university supported by Samsung. Its humanities and social sciences campus is in central Seoul and its natural sciences campus in Suwon, with notable strength in semiconductor engineering, electronics, computing, business and pharmacy.

International students apply through SKKU's global admissions office for March or September entry with school records, a study plan and TOPIK or English scores. Admission and merit scholarships are available.
sungkyunkwan-university-skku.aid_intl: Admission and merit scholarships for international students (partial to full tuition), plus GKS.
sungkyunkwan-university-skku.tests: No SAT/ACT requirement (international results may be submitted as supporting evidence). Korean-taught programmes require TOPIK (usually level 3–4 or higher); English-taught tracks require TOEFL/IELTS or equivalent. Exact minimums are set in each semester's admission guideline.
sungkyunkwan-university-skku.gpa_note: Holistic document review; strong school records expected.
requirements: Passport and nationality documents of applicant and parents
Bank statement for the D-2 visa

technische-universitat-wien.about:
TU Wien was founded in 1815 and has campuses across central Vienna, including the historic Karlsplatz main building. It has eight faculties covering architecture and planning, civil and environmental engineering, informatics, physics, chemistry, mathematics, electrical engineering and mechanical engineering, with strong research in materials, quantum physics and computing.

International applicants with foreign school-leaving certificates apply online within fixed windows (for non-EU citizens, closing 15 January for the summer semester and 15 July for the winter semester) and must reach German C1. Tuition follows the low Austrian public-university rate.
technische-universitat-wien.aid_intl: Few scholarships for international bachelor's students; some OeAD grants and fee waivers for certain countries.
technische-universitat-wien.tests: No SAT/ACT. Bachelor's programmes are taught in German: proof of German at A2 to apply and C1 before admission (the university preparation programme VWU can help). Some foreign certificates require supplementary exams; some programmes (e.g. informatics, architecture) have admission procedures.
technische-universitat-wien.gpa_note: Admission requires a recognised school-leaving certificate; selection procedures apply to some programmes.
requirements: Secondary qualification equivalent to the Austrian Matura (supplementary exams if not)
German A2 to apply, C1 before admission
Programme pre-phase/admission procedure for some programmes
Proof of funds for the Austrian residence permit
